request.spec:
A hold now has a from-date (default the sheet's today) and an optional to-date, and a person may
have several holds over time. Only a person's OPEN claims dated within a hold are left out of the
live totals; their other open claims count, and a claim bound by a statement stays in the totals
whatever its date. Show hold yes/no as whether the person has any hold. Holding writes
PERSON_HELD name=<name> from=<date>; releasing is no longer a separate action (a hold ends on
its to-date).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A hold now has a from-date (default the sheet's today) and an optional to-date, and a person may
have several holds over time. Only a person's OPEN claims dated within a hold are left out of the
live totals; their other open claims count, and a claim bound by a statement stays in the totals
whatever its date. Show hold yes/no as whether the person has any hold. Holding writes
PERSON_HELD name=<name> from=<date>; releasing is no longer a separate action (a hold ends on
its to-date).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Holds now have a from-date and an optional to-date, and a person can have several. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**What changed**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V31__person_hold.sql`, adds a `person_hold` table (from-date required, to-date optional) and drops the old `person.held` yes/no column. Anyone already on hold is carried over as a hold with no start or end date, so their totals don't change.
- **Server:**
  - **Hold action:** the existing hold endpoint now takes `{from, to}` and adds a hold. A blank from-date means the sheet's today. It writes `PERSON_HELD sheet=… by=… name=… from=<date>`, and `PERSON_RELEASED` is gone. Each person returned by the API now lists their holds instead of the old yes/no flag.
  - **The rule:** a claim is left out of the live totals only if it is OPEN, dated within one of the person's holds (both end dates included), and not bound by a statement. This one rule now drives the rollup and its audit lines and closing a period. Statements use part of it, as explained below.
- **Front end:** each person's row has "Hold from" and "Hold to" date fields and a Hold button, plus a list showing one line per hold. "On hold" shows yes when the person has any hold, whatever the dates. The screen's own totals use the same rule as the server.

**Choices the request didn't settle:**
- **PENDING claims now count while held.** Before, a hold left out both OPEN and PENDING claims. The request says only OPEN ones are left out, so I followed that.
- **New statements leave out held claims.** A statement taken during a hold doesn't bind an OPEN claim dated within it, even if an earlier statement had bound it. That claim then becomes unbound and drops out of the totals. The other way round, keeping it bound, would also be reasonable; it's a one-line change in `StatementService.take` if you prefer that.
- **Backwards holds are refused.** A to-date before the from-date returns 400 and shows the row's error. The tests don't check this.

There's no way to end or remove a hold after it's added, since the request says a hold ends on its to-date.
